{"assignees":[],"author":"FiraSenax","base":"main","body":"Tenant-controlled values in 14 Agent ID checks are HTML-encoded but still interpreted as Markdown in the report. A display name can become a disguised link, add formatting, or disappear into an image element. Apply `Get-MtSafeMarkdown` at 39 output sites covering names, UPNs, roles, groups, resource names, redirect URIs and descriptions, including passing observation tables. Let the helper handle pipes and line breaks. Retain HTML encoding before Markdown escaping so names containing literal entities such as `©` keep their original text. Addresses #2711. These are the 14 remaining checks listed there; MT.1260 already adopted the helper in #2710. Validation on macOS, PowerShell 7.5.2 and Pester 5.7.1: - Added 136 fixture cases exercising the actual native check functions. On unchanged main `34e16ef4`, 122 fail and 14 pass; all 136 pass with this patch. Cases cover disguised links, images, formatting, bare URLs, www URLs, email addresses, pipes/line breaks and literal HTML entities in findings and custom-role observations. - All 244 focused Agent ID/helper tests passed. - Full unit wrapper passed in a clean temporary checkout with the exact patch: **191 files, 8,642 cases — 8,549 passed, 93 skipped, zero failures**. This includes 1,700 ScriptAnalyzer cases. The native metadata of all 14 changed checks is identical to main. - Module build and packaged-module validation passed. - Rendered the captured results with the report's locked Marked 18.1.3 and DOMPurify 3.4.17, its GFM/raw-HTML settings and image hook, using JSDOM 31.0.0. Before the fix, 84 of 136 cases produced links, 17 produced image elements, and 64 changed the supplied text. After the fix, every supplied value remains literal, no link/image elements are injected, and all table rows retain their column counts. All inputs in the regression and renderer checks are synthetic. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Entra security reports now safely render names, reasons, permissions, and other values containing Markdown-sensitive characters, links, or line breaks. * Corrected the displayed formatting of user principal names in excessive-access findings. * **Tests** * Added coverage for Markdown rendering across Entra Agent findings and observations. Don't recreate it. **Why:** He wants PR review to stay in the GitHub flow, with one place to act. **How to apply:** For "review PR N", give findings and a draft comment in chat; post it to GitHub only after he approves the text. Rulings that still hold: - Assign the author when a PR waits on them; remove them on approve or merge. - The main ruleset has `require_last_push_approval`: after Merill pushes to a PR, his approval no longer counts. Prefer asking the author to fix or merge main; push to a contributor's branch only when he asks for that fix. - Review comments, approvals above all, are short and informal. Don't restate what the author did, and don't say "exactly what I asked for" or "this is exactly the split". A thanks, the verdict and any optional notes are enough. - CIS checks follow the benchmark's PowerShell audit procedure (scope, values, missing data); quote the audit from `~/Downloads/REDACTED.0.0.pdf` before asking an author to change scope. The agent checks MT.1200–1213 still have it in their titles, but that's legacy and due for cleanup, not the convention to copy. The same goes for their outer try/catch: native tests let the engine handle 403s and errors. **Why:** On 2026-10-18 I asked the author of PR 2401 (MT.1225) to add "(Preview)" to match MT.1210. That reversed Merill's own 16 Oct review, which had asked for it to be removed. Merill deleted my comment as invalid. **How to apply:** Before reviewing a PR, read the existing reviews and comments on it, including the maintainer's own, and don't contradict a change they already asked for. Don't treat the agent tests MT.1200–1213 as the pattern for new checks.

﻿function Get-MtSafeMarkdown {
    <#
	.SYNOPSIS
		Escapes text to be safe to use in markdown.

	.DESCRIPTION
		Escapes text to be safe to use in markdown.

		Use this for any value that comes from the tenant (display names, app names, policy names, etc.)
		before inserting it into test result markdown. Without it, a value such as an app registration
		named '![x](https://attacker.example/pixel.png)' or '[Sign in again](https://phish.example)' would be
		rendered by the report as a remote image or a clickable link, and a '|' would break table layout.

		Characters with meaning in markdown are backslash-escaped, and so are the ones that make GFM
		turn text into a link on its own: a bare 'https://host', 'ftp://host', 'www.host', 'a@b' or
		'mailto:a@b' is an autolink literal, not markdown syntax, and the report renders with
		'gfm: true'. Line breaks are replaced with spaces. Every backslash added here is consumed by
		the renderer, so the value is displayed exactly as entered.

	.PARAMETER Text
		The text to escape

	.EXAMPLE
		PS C:\> Get-MtSafeMarkdown -Text $tenantName

		Converts the content of $tenantName into something safe to use in markdown.

	.EXAMPLE
		PS C:\> "| [$(Get-MtSafeMarkdown $app.displayName)]($portalLink) |"

		Uses a tenant-controlled app name as link text in a markdown table row.

	.LINK
		https://maester.dev/docs/commands/Get-MtSafeMarkdown
	#>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([string])]
    param (
        [Parameter(Position = 0)]
        [AllowNull()]
        [AllowEmptyString()]
        [string]
        $Text
    )
    Write-Verbose "Escaping markdown text."
    if ([string]::IsNullOrEmpty($Text)) { return $Text }

    # Keep values on a single line so they can't start new markdown blocks or table rows.
    $Text = $Text -replace '\r\n|\r|\n', ' '
    # Two passes, and the order matters. The first escapes every character that is either
    # markdown syntax or part of an autolink literal; it runs once, so the backslashes it
    # adds are never escaped again. The second handles the one autolink form that contains
    # no such character: GFM links a bare `www.host`, so the dot after `www` is escaped
    # too. It cannot double-escape, because it only ever matches a dot. There is
    # deliberately no word boundary before `www`: GFM accepts `_` immediately before the
    # `www.`, and `_` is a word character, so `\bwww` does not match `_www.` - the first
    # pass escapes the underscore, the renderer consumes that backslash, and the link comes
    # back. Escaping the dot in any `www.` is harmless: in `awww.host`, which GFM does not
    # autolink anyway, the extra backslash is consumed by the renderer.
    #
    # `:` and `@` are not markdown syntax. They are here because the report renders with
    # `gfm: true`, so `https://host`, `ftp://host`, `mailto:a@b` and a bare `a@b` in a
    # tenant-controlled name each render as a live link without them. A plain `contoso.com`
    # is deliberately left alone: GFM does not autolink it, and escaping every dot would be
    # noise in the JSON output for no gain.
    ($Text -replace '([\\`*_\[\]()!|<>~:@])', '\$1') -replace '(?<=www)\.', '\.'
}

content.text:
I'd approve [maester365/maester#2774](https://github.com/maester365/maester/pull/2774). It's a clean follow-up to #2711, and I found nothing that blocks it.

**What it does:** in MT.1200–1213 and MT.1223, each value that comes from the tenant used to go through `HtmlEncode` plus a manual pipe and line-break replace. Now it goes through `Get-MtSafeMarkdown -Text (HtmlEncode …)`. That covers display names, UPNs, role names, reasons, redirect URIs and permissions, including the passing-observation tables in 1207, 1209 and 1210.

**Checked:**
- **Order of the two steps is right.** HtmlEncode runs first, so entities like `©` stay literal. The entities it produces (`&`, `<`, `'`) contain no character `Get-MtSafeMarkdown` escapes, so nothing gets escaped twice. A `|` survives HtmlEncode and comes out as `\|`.
- **The `(unnamed)` fallback still works** where it now runs after escaping (1203, 1207, 1209, 1210), because the helper returns an empty string for empty input.
- **Columns left unescaped are values the check writes itself:** IDs, ObjectType, PrivilegeType, Kind, AttackPath, and the fixed Reason text in 1200 and 1201. The 1209 Scope column is a directory scope ID. None of these come from tenant names.
- **The one changed existing assertion is expected.** `au1\@ contoso.com` is the new `@` escaping.
- **Attributes are unchanged**, and the attribute-review check passed.
- **CI is green** on all three OSes. There are no other reviews; CodeRabbit had no findings.

**Optional nit:** `Test-MtEntraAgentMarkdown.Tests.ps1` takes a `param([string] $MarkdownCapturePath)`, and the AfterEach/AfterAll code collects results to write to that file. That only served the author's renderer check outside the repo, so it's noise here. Removing it also clears one of the three code-scanning alerts on the file. The other two (`findingCases` and `observationCases` "unused") are false positives: Pester uses those variables through `-ForEach`.

**Draft comment** (not posted yet):

> Thanks @FiraSenax — nice, thorough fix, and good call keeping the HtmlEncode before the escape so literal entities survive. Approving.
>
> Optional: the `MarkdownCapturePath` param and the capture plumbing in `Test-MtEntraAgentMarkdown.Tests.ps1` were only for your out-of-repo renderer check, so feel free to drop them (that also clears the code-scanning alert). Happy to merge either way.
